decision.case_state: Ticket NBL-012 (dishwasher door, Flat 9, 89 Juniper Mews) is at visit stage, routine severity. Landlord agreed for an engineer to attend (events 008, 012). Riverside Compliance was assigned (event 013/015). Tenant reports all troubleshooting checks done and door still not closing (event 011). Visit is not confirmed: the tenant was called by "Grant from Cedar Utilities" about Wed 29/04 8-12, which does not match the assigned contractor. Ticket is on hold, waiting for the provider, review 2026-04-28.

next_actions.action: Ask Riverside Compliance to confirm whether Cedar Utilities/Grant is their engineer, that they can attend Wed 29/04/2026 8am-12pm, and that the tenant is Leo Turner. Told them not to attend until confirmed in writing.
Tell tenant the Wed 29 April 8am-12pm visit is being confirmed with the contractor, and that we will text once confirmed.
Hold ticket NBL-012 as Waiting for Provider; review on 2026-04-28 and set the visit only once the contractor confirms.

boundaries: Sending the request to the contractor and the tenant does not confirm the visit, the engineer's identity, or the cause of the fault.
No set_visit booking has been made, so the 29/04 08:00 slot in event 017 is not a confirmed booking.
No repair quote exists, so approval for the repair cost is not established.
The landlord's approval covers an engineer attending to investigate and repair if possible; it sets no spend cap and that is not recorded.
remaining_work: Riverside Compliance to confirm the engineer, company and the 29/04 slot (review 2026-04-28).
Once confirmed, book the visit with set_visit (access: tenant_home, per the slot) and notify tenant and contractor.
After the visit, record the work result and any quote; the repair cost needs landlord approval if above any limit (none recorded).
Chase landlord (Imogen Oakley / Maya Kendall) if a quote is needed.
missing_info: Identity of the caller 'Grant from Cedar Utilities' and whether they are Riverside Compliance's engineer.
Landlord spend limit for the dishwasher repair (property record has none).
Confirmation of tenant name: 'Leo Turner' (event 014/015) vs 'Leo Kendall' (event 016).
Current contractor's written confirmation of the 29/04 slot.
decision.summary: The dishwasher door job NBL-012 is at visit stage and the landlord agreed to an engineer attending. The visit is not confirmed because a caller from "Cedar Utilities" offered a slot on Wed 29/04 8am-12pm, but the assigned contractor is Riverside Compliance and the tenant name differs. I placed the ticket on hold until 2026-04-28, asked Riverside to confirm, and told the tenant we are checking the visit.

answers.question: 1. Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Routine job at visit stage. Tenant reports the door still will not close after the checks (event 011). Riverside Compliance is assigned (events 013/015). The visit is unconfirmed: the Cedar Utilities call and the 08:00 slot in event 017 do not match the assigned contractor. Outstanding: contractor confirmation of the engineer and slot, the visit booking, the attendance result, and any repair quote and approval.

answers.question: 2. What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Email Riverside Compliance (existing thread, event 015) to confirm the engineer, company, slot and tenant name. SMS Leo Turner on 07700 900763 that the visit is being confirmed and we will text once it is. Hold NBL-012 until 2026-04-28.

answers.question: 3. Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No urgent decision now. The routine repair is within the landlord's agreed scope. Escalate only if Riverside cannot confirm the visit, or if the repair quote exceeds the landlord's approval, or if the Cedar Utilities caller turns out to be an unknown third party.
